validated_work_order.understanding: A custom report's conditions button is icon-only: CompactFiltersButton renders a bare Button whose only child is SvgFilter, with no text node and no aria-label, so its accessible name is empty. The e2e page model works around that by enumerating every button in the report page, skipping any with an aria-label or non-empty text, and clicking the first one whose bounding box sits right of x=850 (custom-report-page.ts:55-77). That is the only way the suite reaches the conditions menu, and it is why four call sites in reports.test.ts each carry their own copy of selectOnlyBillsGroup and switchToAnyOf. The fix is to give the button a name and locate it by that name. This is the third planning pass; both objections from the second rejection are answered explicitly in the fields below.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The control has no accessible name, and the locator that had to compensate for that compensates with geometry. The x>850 threshold is a function of the fixed-width content to the button's left, not of viewport width: ReportTopbar renders nine GraphButtons, three 1px dividers and a SnapshotButton, all flexShrink: 0, then a SpaceBetween with flex:1 and justifyContent:'space-between' (ReportTopbar.tsx:227-233) whose first child is the compact FilterButton. Inside a space-between row the first child sits at the region's left edge, so narrowing the window pushes SaveReport right rather than moving the filter button left. What does follow from the code is that 850 is a fragile sum of sidebar widths (ReportSidebar minWidth 225, SidebarShell MIN_SIDEBAR_WIDTH 200) with little slack, and that a control with no name cannot be addressed at all except by such a sum.
validated_work_order.approach: Add aria-label={t('Filters')} to the existing bare Button in CompactFiltersButton, reusing the translation key the sibling tooltip already uses (FiltersMenu.tsx:744) and matching the pattern every other icon-only control in the topbar uses (GraphButton.tsx:42, SnapshotButton.tsx:45). An aria-label adds no rendered node, so no VRT snapshot moves. Then reduce openConditionsMenu to a single getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click(), which deletes the button scan, the hasName probe, the boundingBox call, the x>850 comparison and the now-unreachable throw, and hoist the two duplicated e2e helpers to the body of the 'custom reports' describe. Because no CI-executed check touches packages/desktop-client/e2e/ (config.yml:172 e2e is empty, vitest includes only src/**, desktop-client tsconfig excludes e2e), the e2e suite is not a gate and is treated throughout as a local-only run in qa_script; the CI-executed backing for the accessible name is a new unit test under src/, and the page-model and suite criteria are stated as structural properties checkable by reading, never as a suite nobody runs.

files.change: Import useTranslation from 'react-i18next' (after the existing React import, matching FiltersMenu.tsx:6), call const { t } = useTranslation(); at the top of CompactFiltersButton, and pass aria-label={t('Filters')} to the existing <Button variant="bare" onPress={onPress} style={{ minWidth: 20 }}>. Nothing else changes: the SvgFilter child, the minWidth, the bare variant and the onPress plumbing stay exactly as they are, and no text node is introduced.
files.why: This is the root of the ticket. 'Filters' is already a translation key in this feature (the tooltip content at FiltersMenu.tsx:744), so no new string enters the catalog and `yarn generate:i18n` output is unaffected. aria-label rather than a visually-hidden span or a title attribute, because aria-label is the pattern already used by the neighbouring icon-only toolbar buttons and adds no DOM node, hence no layout shift and no VRT movement.

files.change: Replace the entire body of openConditionsMenu with one statement: await this.pageContent.getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click();. Delete the buttons/count loop, the hasName probe, the boundingBox() call, the box.x > 850 comparison and the unreachable throw. Rewrite the JSDoc to say the button is addressed by its accessible name rather than by its position among the topbar buttons. Keep the method name, signature and pageContent receiver - reports.test.ts calls it at :291 and :458 and this is its only definition.
files.why: Once the control has a name, the geometric scan is not just fragile but actively harmful: it skips every named button, so it would silently pick a different control the moment the toolbar gains any named button. exact:true keeps the compact and non-compact variants distinguishable - the accounts page's sibling is named 'Filter' (FiltersButton.tsx:13, used at account-page.ts:56), and Playwright's default name matching is substring-based.

files.why: The duplication is what made openConditionsMenu's four callers expensive to fix - each one carried private copies of the two helpers, so the same edit had to be reasoned about in four places. The new test exists because IAC-6 asks for the suite to hold at a narrower width, and it is described as what it is: a positive assertion that the role-and-name locator resolves at 1024px. It is green before and after this change and is not claimed as a regression test for the old scan. The finally that restores the viewport is defensive tidiness so the test is self-contained, NOT protection against cross-test leakage: the outer beforeEach at :23-24 opens a fresh page with browser.newPage() and afterEach at :35-37 closes it, so every test starts at Playwright's default viewport because playwright.config.ts `use:` (:16-24) sets no viewport key - and the pre-existing :177 already sets 1280x700 unrestored with no effect on the toMatchThemeScreenshots cases at :667 and :675 that run after it.

risks: The e2e suite is not a gate. Nothing CI executes touches packages/desktop-client/e2e/ - config.yml:172 has e2e: "", vitest includes only src/** (vite.config.mts:405), and desktop-client's tsconfig excludes e2e - so the page-model and reports.test.ts changes can only be validated by a local playwright run. This checkout has no node_modules, so no test, lint, typecheck or Playwright run was executed while planning. Every claim above about current behaviour is read from source, and the two behaviours that could not be checked by running are called out in unknowns[] rather than asserted.

exact:true on the name means a translation of 'Filters' in a non-English locale no longer matches. Playwright runs against the dev server's default locale, and the pre-existing locator was locale-independent; if e2e is ever run under a translated locale this needs the English string or a test id.

Hoisting two helpers into the 'custom reports' describe body changes when they are constructed relative to the nested describes. They are plain const arrow functions closing over only `page` and `customReportPage`, both of which are assigned by beforeEach hooks that run after the describe body is evaluated but before any test body - so the closure reads them at call time, exactly as it did before. This is a scoping change only, but it is why the diff touches three regions of a 700-line file and the local Playwright run in qa_script is not optional.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give the button a visually hidden text node instead of an aria-label (a <Text> with a screen-reader-only style).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It adds a DOM node to a bare button with an explicit minWidth: 20, which is the kind of thing that moves pixels and invalidates visual-regression snapshots for no accessibility gain over aria-label. aria-label is what the neighbouring GraphButton and SnapshotButton already do.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the positional scan but widen or recompute the threshold, or scan for the button next to a known landmark.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves the control without an accessible name, which is the actual defect: the button is announced to a screen reader as just "button". Fixing the locator instead of the name treats the symptom.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a data-testid to CompactFiltersButton and point the page model at it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves the accessible name empty. The repo's convention for icon-only toolbar controls is aria-label (GraphButton.tsx:42, SnapshotButton.tsx:45), and there are already established name-based e2e locators (account-page.ts:56). The ticket explicitly prefers a hook a person benefits from.

alternatives_considered.approach: Also wrap the pre-existing setViewportSize at reports.test.ts:177 in a try/finally while the file is being edited.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is unrelated to the ticket and would make AC-6 assert something this change does not control. The objection that forced the AC-6 rewrite was precisely that the old criterion claimed a file-wide property the diff did not establish; repeating that in a different form would be the same error. Leaving :177 untouched and stating the two-hit expectation in AC-6 is the honest version.

assumptions: t('Filters') returns the literal string 'Filters' under the desktop-client vitest environment, because TestProviders (src/mocks.tsx:42-61) supplies no I18nextProvider and react-i18next falls back to the key. Supported by the sibling FiltersMenu.test.tsx, which asserts literal English such as 'Apply' under the same wrapper.
The dev server used by Playwright runs in English; the suite already asserts literal English strings.

'Filters' is a better name than the sibling's singular 'Filter' because the control opens a list of filters and because the tooltip on this very control already says 'Filters' - introducing a second string would mean a second key for one button.
unknowns: Whether the old x>850 scan actually failed at any narrower width. It does not follow from the source: the button is the first child of a flex:1 space-between SpaceBetween (ReportTopbar.tsx:227-234), so its left edge is fixed by the flexShrink:0 siblings to its left, and narrowing the window moves SaveReport right rather than the filter button left. Relatedly, isNarrowWidth is width < 512 (tokens.ts small: 512) and gates the whole ReportTopbar at CustomReport.tsx:930, so a genuinely narrow width removes the button instead of relocating it. Verifying either would need a checkout with node_modules and a browser; until then the new 1024px case is claimed only as a positive assertion that the locator resolves by role and name.

Whether the VRT snapshots in reports.test.ts are byte-identical after adding an aria-label. They should be - aria-label renders nothing - but only a local `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run vrt` confirms it, and VRT is not a CI gate either.
